newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan nets 100 illegal Chinese immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Japan nets 100 illegal Chinese immigrants.

text.p: Japan has arrested 100 Chinese off the central port city of Nagoya in the biggest haul of illegal immigrants in recent years, a Maritime Safety Agency official said on Thursday.
"We arrested 100 Chinese on suspicion of illegal entry... This is the biggest group arrest in years," agency spokesman Satoshi Sato said.
"The group was found on a fishing vessel in the Ise gulf, south of Nagoya," Sato said.
Maritime safety officials patrolling the gulf spotted a Japanese fishing boat alongside a 100-tonne Chinese vessel 13 nautical miles offshore on Tuesday night, he said.
Officials boarded both vessels and found 64 Chinese hiding in the fish hold of the 19.75-tonne Maneimaru and 36 elsewhere on the vessel, Sato said.
"We arrested 77 men and 23 women...and detained the four Japanese crew on suspicion of aiding and abetting," he said. The arrests took place on Wednesday.
Most Chinese illegal immigrants enter Japan from the southeastern Chinese province of Fujian, west of Taiwan, Sato said. The origin of the 100 was still under investigation, he said.

Chinese illegal immigrants often enter Japan by hiding in containers transported by large container ships, or by transferring on the high seas from a Chinese vessel to a Japanese fishing boat heading for home, Sato said.
So far this year, a record 401 illegal immigrants were intercepted by maritime safety officials, more than double last year's 164 arrests, he said.
